Lviv Old Jewish Cemetery on Shpytalna Street

Jewish Cemetery · L'vivs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This is one of at least four documented Jewish cemeteries in Lviv, a city whose Jewish and Karaite communities date to its mid-13th-century founding and which became a major center of Haskalah, Hasidism, Zionism, and Jewish printing — birthplace of the chess grandmaster Alexander Beliavsky and mathematician Mark Vishik, and site of the Janowska concentration camp, documented at length elsewhere in this collection. This particular cemetery, appearing on Polish maps from the 1930s, has no visible traces remaining today; the Krakivskyy marketplace and the yard of the City Hospital now occupy the site.
